Class RegionRegistry

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.inject.RegionRegistry
@Internal public final class RegionRegistry extends Object
Internal registry mapping M5 regions to their registered panels. Holds process-lifetime state; panels register once at mod init (typically during adapter/builder construction) and remain registered until process exit. See M5 design doc §6.1 for the singleton contract and §6.1a for ordering semantics. See M5 design doc §12.5a for the padding + diagnostic additions from Phase 12.5.

Not pure. Stacking depends on registration order and per-frame visibility. The pure math lives in RegionMath; this class supplies the prefix input to that math by walking its panel lists, and owns the state needed for one-shot overflow diagnostics.

Internal only. Consumers don't call this directly — the MenuContext ScreenPanelAdapter overload and the HUD panel builder register and resolve on their behalf.

  • Field Details

    • NOT_REGISTERED

      public static final int NOT_REGISTERED
      Sentinel returned by the axialPrefix variants when self is not found in its region list — i.e. the panel was unregistered (or never registered) but a stale per-screen dispatch reference still reached the resolver this frame.

      The render/input path MUST treat this as ScreenOrigin.OUT_OF_REGION (skip the panel) rather than crashing. A geometry resolver on the per-frame path may never throw — an uncaught throw inside a screen's render or click loop wedges that screen's entire input. The condition is transient (it resolves on the next frame once the stale reference is dropped), so we degrade silently.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • registerMenu

      public static void registerMenu(Panel panel, MenuRegion region, int padding, int priority)
      Registers a MenuContext panel into a region with a content padding and explicit priority. Called from the ScreenPanelAdapter region constructor. Padding participates in axial-prefix stacking and overflow math; priority + captured modId drive the deterministic sort order applied at axialPrefix(Panel, MenuRegion) time.

    • registerMenu

      public static void registerMenu(Panel panel, MenuRegion region)
      Back-compatible overload for consumers registering without the padding extension. Delegates with ScreenPanelAdapter.DEFAULT_PADDING so behavior matches the default-padding adapter constructors.

    • unregisterMenu

      public static void unregisterMenu(Panel panel)
      Removes a previously-registered MenuContext panel from every region list it appears in and clears its per-panel metadata (padding, priority, modId, registration sequence, overflow warning state).

      Phase 16j R5 — the registry was append-only prior to this. Use via ScreenPanelAdapter.unregister(); this method is the registry-side primitive. Idempotent: unregistering a non-registered panel is a no-op.

      After unregister, the panel can be re-registered with a fresh registerMenu(Panel, MenuRegion, int, int) call (e.g., via constructing a new adapter).

    • axialPrefix

      public static int axialPrefix(Panel self, MenuRegion region)
      Computes the axial stacking prefix for a panel — total extent (plus gap) contributed by visible preceding panels in the same region. Each panel's axial extent includes its registered padding. Panels registered before self that are hidden in the current frame contribute zero, so the stack collapses naturally.

      Phase 16i: iteration order is a deterministic sort, not registration order. Sort key is (priority asc, modId asc, registrationSeq asc) — lower priority renders first (closer to the region's anchor edge), with modId as the natural tiebreaker for two consumers sharing a priority and registration sequence as a final stabilizer for two panels from the same mod with the same priority.

      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if self is not registered in region

    • resolveMenuOrigin

      public static ScreenOrigin resolveMenuOrigin(Panel panel, @Nullable MenuRegion region, ScreenBounds bounds, net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?> screen)
      Resolves the screen-space origin for a MenuContext panel. Consults the registry (for the stacking prefix and the panel's registered padding), the current ScreenBounds (for the menu frame), and MenuChrome.of(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen) (for chrome extents outside the declared frame), producing a screen-space origin — or ScreenOrigin.OUT_OF_REGION when the panel overflows its region.

      Chrome-extended bounds are computed once per frame and passed to RegionMath. Math stays pure; chrome logic lives here.

      Parameters:
      region - the declared region anchor — null for a pixel-positioned panel (the PIXEL branch below returns before any region use)

    • resolveAround

      public static ScreenOrigin resolveAround(Panel panel, MenuRegion region, ScreenBounds frame, int pad, int prefix, int sw, int sh)
      The frame-relative region resolution CORE, shared by the vanilla-injection path (resolveMenuOrigin(Panel, MenuRegion, ScreenBounds, AbstractContainerScreen), frame = the menu frame) and the custom- screen path (Movement ③ — frame = the screen's MAIN panel bounds, fed by MainRegionLayout). Given a frame in screen coordinates it applies, identically in both contexts:
      • the single overlay rule (①) — an overlay panel ignores its region and floats centred on the SCREEN WINDOW (drawn on top via the pass split in ScreenPanelRegistry.renderMatchingPanels(AbstractContainerScreen, GuiGraphicsExtractor, int, int));
      • the both-axis screen-edge budgets — ① width + ② height — fed BEFORE measuring so the panel wraps/auto-scrolls to fit the room its anchor leaves toward the screen edge;
      • RegionMath.resolveMenu(MenuRegion, ScreenBounds, int, int, int, int, int) for the final anchored origin.
      Returns ScreenOrigin.OUT_OF_REGION when the panel can't be placed.
      Parameters:
      frame - the anchor frame in screen coords (the menu frame, or the custom screen's main-panel bounds)
      pad - the panel's content padding (added around getWidth/getHeight)
      prefix - axial stacking offset of preceding visible same-region siblings

    • feedRegionBudget

      public static void feedRegionBudget(Panel panel, MenuRegion region, ScreenBounds frame, int pad, int sw, int sh)
      The reactive-sizing step of the ONE region engine — shared verbatim by the vanilla-injection path (resolveAround(Panel, MenuRegion, ScreenBounds, int, int, int, int), frame = the menu frame) and the custom-screen path (MainRegionLayout, frame = the MAIN panel's bounds). Feeds panel its anchor-aware width (①) + height (②) budget — the room its region's anchor edge leaves toward the screen edge, against frame — BEFORE the caller measures it, so the panel wraps/auto-scrolls to fit instead of overflowing. An overlay panel ignores its region and gets the symmetric centred-screen width budget (it floats centred on the screen window).

      This is the single place a region panel learns how much room it has; both the vanilla menu and a custom screen feed it identically. There is no vanilla-vs-custom split in the resize engine — only the frame (menu frame vs main-panel bounds) differs, which is the whole point of Movement ③.

    • unregisterHud

      public static void unregisterHud(MKHudPanelDef def)
      Removes a previously-registered HUD panel def from every region list it appears in and clears its per-def metadata. Phase 16j R5. Idempotent. Symmetric counterpart to registerHud(MKHudPanelDef, HudRegion, int).

      Note: this does NOT unregister the HUD panel def from MK's top-level HUD list (the render-each-frame collection). Use MK.unregisterHud(def) for that.

    • axialPrefix

      public static int axialPrefix(MKHudPanelDef self, HudRegion region)
      Axial prefix for a HUD panel. All HUD regions flow vertically, so the prefix is the sum of preceding visible panels' heights plus gaps.

      Phase 16i: iteration order is sorted by (priority, modId, registrationSeq) — same semantic as the MenuContext path.

      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if self is not registered in region

    • registerVanillaScreen

      public static void registerVanillaScreen(Panel panel, ScreenRegion region, int padding, int priority)
      Registers a VanillaScreenContext panel into a region with explicit padding + priority. Called from VanillaScreenPanelAdapter's region constructor. Padding participates in axial-prefix stacking (panel's reported size + 2× padding contributes to subsequent siblings' offset); priority + captured modId drive deterministic sort.
